Mina: Quick flag: veridian-lite-v2:q5 nightly shows BLEU regression on ja->zh (~-2.2) focused on parenthetical furigana. Attaching a tiny repro.
Cheng: short? tokenization or model-decoding?
Mina: looks like token boundary differences. baseline (fp32) tokenizes "大阪(おおさか)" as ["大阪","(","おおさか",")"] but q5 run shows char-split kana inside parentheses.
EvalBot: auto-report: dataset=news_locale_ja_zh, n=200, BLEU baseline=24.3 -> q5=22.1, chrF drop -0.029. top mismatches grouped by parenthetical_furigana slice.
Julian: paste exact tokenizer outputs + environment (sentencepiece version, wheel).
Mina: ran harness with --show-tokenization. Commands:
```
python -m eval.harness --model veridian-lite-v2:fp32 --split sample_42 --show-tokenization
python -m eval.harness --model veridian-lite-v2:q5 --split sample_42 --show-tokenization
```
input: "大阪(おおさか)に到着した。"
fp32 tokens: ["大阪","(","おおさか",")","に","到着","した","。"]
q5 tokens: ["大","阪","(","お","お","さ","か",")",...]

Rina: checking bundles: both manifests list tokenizer.sha=abc123. But quant runtime loads /opt/tokenizers from our wheel which is sentencepiece 0.1.99; baseline container uses 0.1.97.
Cheng: minor SP versions sometimes change unicode normalization (NFKC/NFC) or pre-token normalization rules. Mixed Han+Kana combos are fragile.
Julian: plan: 1) reproduce tokenization using model .model file inside quant container (no model load) 2) pin sentencepiece to 0.1.97 in a minimal q5 image and rerun harness 3) try forcing tokenizer normalization flags when exporting tokenizer.
Mina: I did step (1) inside container: `python -c "from sentencepiece import SentencePieceProcessor; p=SentencePieceProcessor(); p.Load('tokenizer.model'); print(p.encode_as_pieces(text))"` -> it produced the split only when run in the full quant image, not when I ran the same command locally with the same tokenizer.model. So binary ABI or linked libdifferences likely.
EvalBot: historical note: similar incident referenced 1749204321 where SP bump caused token boundary diffs. Crosslinking.
Rina: building ci image that pins sp=0.1.97 now. If that reverts token boundaries we'll either pin or bake normalization into exported tokenizer.proto.
Mina: workaround: runtime decoding fallback rule for canary traffic: if detected CJK+kana parenthetical spans with token count > 1 more than baseline threshold, route to fp32 pool. Slow but keeps canary healthy.
Cheng: approve fallback. Also add nightly regression alert: ja->zh BLEU delta > 1.0.
Julian: add onboarding gate: any quant image must pass a token-boundary parity smoke test with 100 ja samples that include furigana/parentheses. Add manifest check to assert sentencepiece version or embedded norm string.

Julian: thanks everyone. keep updates here. :thumbsup:
